messages:
From: Alex Stone <alex.stone@seabreeze-retail.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: Checkout failures + 5xx spike across US region

Hi Stephanie / Jordan,

We're seeing a rapid increase in 5xx errors and checkout latency across the US region starting around 08:40 PDT. Impact: 18% of checkout attempts failing (users see spinner then error), pages with complex recommendations have ~8s median latency (normally <400ms). Traffic pattern looks normal; this started when they rolled a query optimizer at 08:30 on our side.

Can Redwood join an incident bridge? We need immediate mitigation and an ETA for a fix — this is driving CX escalations.

--
Alex Stone
Head of Platform Engineering
Seabreeze Retail
alex.stone@seabreeze-retail.com

Alex — thanks for the flag and for the samples. We're on a quick bridge at 09:45 PDT (link sent to ops). Plan for the first 30 minutes: triage -> short mitigation -> agreement on rollback or patch.

Proposed mitigation (short-lived):
- Apply short-fuse throttling for non-critical recommendation reads to reduce tail latency (5–10 min).
- Increase KV cache warm-up parallelism for Seabreeze customer shards.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-20T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Initial diagnostic: KV cache warming + batching edge case

Triage summary (10:00 PDT):
- Symptoms: heavy tail latency on recommendation model shards causing dependent checkout microservice to time out. Error pattern: request ids show blocked forward progress at tokenization-> KV lookup.
- Root cause hypothesis: a recent optimizer changed request concurrency distribution (larger batching windows) which interacted poorly with KV cache warm-up for new shards; cold cache combined with larger batches produced head-of-line blocking and increased request timeouts.

Immediate corrective actions (approved for canary):
1) Reduce max batch size from 64->32 for affected model group (canary on 2% of traffic).
2) Increase KV prefetch parallelism (config: kv.prefetch=8 -> 16).
3) Add request-level deadline softening to allow retries in calling microservice.

I'll prepare a short playbook and a runnable patch. Need go/no-go for canary from Stephanie and Jordan. More follow-up after data from canary.

-- Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stone <alex.stone@seabreeze-retail.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@seabreeze-retail.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-25T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Delivery: Draft RCA & remediation timeline (Seabreeze)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for patience. Attached is our draft RCA and the remediation trace documenting owners, commits, and verification steps. High-level:
- Root cause: request batching + KV cache warm-up interaction after optimizer change -> head-of-line blocking -> elevated tail latency -> dependent service timeouts and 5xxs.
- Interim mitigations applied 2028-03-20: throttles, canary batch-size rollback, KV prefetch increase.
- Permanent fixes scheduled: runtime safeguard to detect batch-window pathology, improved prefetch heuristics, and a small change to the optimizer gating logic.

Remediation timeline (summary):
- 2028-03-20 10:20 PDT: Canary patch (batch-size, kv.prefetch) rolled to 2% traffic; observed 70% reduction in 95th latency for affected endpoints.
- 2028-03-22 11:00 PDT: Canary expanded to 30%; sustained improvements.
- 2028-03-25 09:00 PDT: Full rollout of emergency patch completed.
- 2028-03-27 02:00 PDT: Permanent safeguard PR merged; verification plan executed in staging.

Attached: 2028-03-25-seabreeze-rca.pdf, throughput-graphs-q1.png, proposed-fix-playbook.md

Action items for Seabreeze (please confirm):
- Confirm acceptable verification windows and SLA thresholds for post-fix monitoring.
- Approve a short maintenance window next Tuesday (03/29) for optimizer gating change if you'd like Redwood to implement it on your behalf.

We will track outstanding action owners in the attached remediation trace; below are owners for the key items:
- Karthik: runtime safeguard + code PR (Complete 03/24)
- David: autoscaling/routing verification + metrics dashboard (Complete 03/26)
- Marissa: customer comms, credits, and SLA remediation proposal (In progress)
- Jordan: executive readout coordination & postmortem acceptance (In progress)

Please review the RCA and call out any questions. If accepted, we'll convert this draft to a final RCA and schedule the executive readout.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
